checkpoints.title: Periodic quotient / physical-lift dictionary
checkpoints.input_contract:
01. T := UnitAddTorus (Fin 3), Vec := EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), pi:Vec->T the unit-period quotient
      map; volume on T has mass one.
  02. Physical lift of f:T->R^3 is f o pi. Unit-periodicity means invariance under every Z^3
      translation. Scalar pressure uses the same quotient.
  03. No mean-zero hypothesis is imposed on the dictionary itself; the mean-zero source predicates
      are specialized only after taking the mean.
checkpoints.output_contract:
01. For every quotient-integrable scalar/vector function f: integral_T f = integral_unitCube (f o
      pi). In particular, L2 norms and means agree.
  02. For every smooth periodic lift F there exists a unique quotient function f with F=f o pi;
      spatial derivatives, divergence, Laplacian, and periodic gradients commute with this
      identification.
  03. For every integrable f and k in Z^3, the quotient Fourier coefficient equals integral_unitCube
      exp(-2*pi*i*k.x)*(f o pi)(x) dx, matching star(fourierCharacter k).
  04. For smooth trajectories restricted to t>=0, construct compatible smooth extensions at t=0
      whenever an actual full time derivative is used by the source contract; restrictions preserve
      the PDE, initial trace, periodicity and pressure mean.
  05. Under zero velocity mean, the dictionary transports the literal fields of
      SingularClosure.SmoothSigmaZero and SingularClosure.GlobalSmoothNSE to their quotient-torus
      predicates. Arbitrary mean remains unrestricted in the general dictionary.

checkpoints.title: Exact cutoff, Leray projector, and real Fourier eigenbasis
checkpoints.input_contract:
01. N in N, N>=1; K_N^0 := {k in Z^3 | k!=0 and sum_i k_i^2<=N^2}; K_N := {0} union K_N^0.
  02. P(k)=I-kk^T/|k|^2 for k!=0; P(0)=I. Pi_N is the Fourier multiplier 1_{K_N}.
  03. V_N is the real divergence-free range of Pi_N; the three standard constant coordinate fields
      are chosen first.
checkpoints.output_contract:
01. K_N^0 = SingularClosure.cutoffModes N and K_N = SingularClosure.sobolevCutoffModes N; the cube
      enumeration in source contains exactly the required Euclidean-ball modes.
  02. P and Pi_N are orthogonal projections on the appropriate L2 spaces, commute with each other,
      all spatial derivatives and A=-Delta, and preserve reality and solenoidality.
  03. There exists a real L2-orthonormal basis (e_j) of V_N consisting of the three constants and
      normalized transverse sine/cosine modes, with A e_j=lambda_j e_j and lambda_j=4*pi^2*|k_j|^2
      for nonconstant modes.
  04. lambda_j>=0, max_j lambda_j<=4*pi^2*N^2, and d_N=3+2*card(K_N^0).
  05. For every basis mode, the physical derivative and Fourier multiplier conventions agree
      literally with CP01.

checkpoints.title: Real-coordinate / constrained-complex isometry and exact drift conjugacy
checkpoints.input_contract:
01. N>=1; q=(m,z) in R^3 x R^(d_N-3), with the standard constant basis fixed by CP02.
  02. Z_N consists of Fourier families c supported in K_N^0 satisfying c(-k)=conj(c(k)) and sum_i
      k_i*c(k,i)=0; its real Hilbert norm is the explicit sum of squared complex coefficients.
  03. I_N(q)=sum_j q_j e_j; C_jkl=integral_T e_j dot ((e_k dot grad)e_l);
      b_nu,N(q)_j=-nu*lambda_j*q_j-sum_kl C_jkl*q_k*q_l, nu>0.
checkpoints.output_contract:
01. There is an explicit real-linear bijection Realify_N:R^(d_N-3)->Z_N such that the zero-mean
      quotient synthesis of Realify_N z equals I_N(0,z).
  02. For c=Realify_N z, |z|^2=SingularClosure.coefficientEnergy N c and
      |q|^2=|m|^2+SingularClosure.coefficientEnergy N c=||I_N(q)||_L2^2.
  03. For every real s, ||I_N(q)||_Hs^2=|m|^2+sum_{k in
      K_N^0}(1+4*pi^2*|k|^2)^s*|c(k)|^2=sum_j(1+lambda_j)^s*q_j^2. The source TorusSobolev norm
      match is specialized to its actual integer s parameter.
  04. For every k in K_N^0: Realify_N(pr_z b_nu,N(m,z))(k)=SingularClosure.galerkinRhs nu N c
      k-2*pi*i*(k dot m)*c(k); pr_m b_nu,N(m,z)=0. The zero extension of the derivative vanishes
      outside K_N^0.
  05. For m=0 the correction term vanishes and the coefficient ODE is exactly the restricted source
      finiteGalerkinRhs. For arbitrary m it is the source zero-mean drift plus the explicit
      constant-advection term.

checkpoints.title: Canonical lift and dense symmetric minimal operator
checkpoints.input_contract:
01. Concrete finite real orthonormal model I_N:R^{d_N}->V_N, smooth polynomial b_N and exact

checkpoints.title: Explicit nonreal resolvents, selfadjoint closure, maximal domains and core
checkpoints.input_contract:
01. Dense symmetric Hmin_N:D_N->Hilbert_N from CP08.
  02. Strongly continuous two-sided unitary group U_N preserving D_N from CP09.
checkpoints.output_contract:
01. H_N=closure(Hmin_N) is densely defined selfadjoint and is the unique selfadjoint extension of
      the actual minimal operator.
  02. For Im z!=0, define sigma_z=sign(Im z), beta_z=|Im z| and R_z
      f=(sigma_z*i/hbar)*integral_0^infinity exp(sigma_z*i*z*t/hbar)*U_N(sigma_z*t)f dt vectorwise;
      ||R_z||<=1/beta_z.
  03. (H_N-z)R_z=Id on all Hilbert_N and R_z(H_N-z)=Id on D(H_N). Both half-plane formulas are
      proved before selfadjointness is concluded.
  04. D(H_N)=D(Hmin_N^*) equals both the maximal adjoint test-pairing domain and the exact strong
      difference-quotient domain; H_N psi=i*hbar times the derivative.
  05. U_N(t)D(H_N)=D(H_N), H_N U_N(t)=U_N(t)H_N there, and U_N(t)psi0 is the unique strong
      Schrodinger solution for psi0 in D(H_N).
  06. The actual C-infinity compact-support D_N is a graph core. For every complex z with Im z!=0,
      ker(Hmin_N^*-z*Id)={0}.
  07. R_z^*=R_conj(z); R_z-R_w=(z-w)R_z R_w; resolvents commute; dR_z/dz=R_z^2 in operator norm.
  08. For C_z=1+(1+|z|)/beta_z, the finite-time resolvent tail is <=C_z*exp(-beta_z*T/hbar)||f|| in
      graph norm. For f_n in D_N approximating (H_N-z)x and T_n->infinity, R_{z,T_n}f_n are actual
      core graph approximants with error (R6.22).
checkpoints.subgoals:
CP10.a | dense_symmetric_graph_closure
    Prove closability from density and symmetry; form the closed symmetric graph closure and its
    nonreal lower bound.
  CP10.b | actual_core_derivative
    Differentiate the explicit weighted pullback in L2 on the actual C-infinity compact core; derive
    TU(t)=U(t)T by the group law.
  CP10.c | vectorwise_resolvents
    Construct both half-plane Bochner integrals, scalar domination, bounded linearity and
    exponential truncation estimates.
  CP10.d | finite_time_graph_and_actual_core
    Integrate the continuous pair (F_z(t)phi,T F_z(t)phi) in the complete closed graph; prove the
    graph identity. Separately prove actual compact smooth support for finite-time core integrals.
  CP10.e | full_space_inverse
    Use test-vector limits and then dense-data graph limits to prove the right inverse; use the
    nonreal lower bound for the left inverse.
  CP10.f | selfadjoint_from_two_ranges
    For v in D(A*), subtract R_z(A*-z)v; the residual is orthogonal to Ran(A-conj(z))=Hilbert_N,
    hence zero. Conclude A*=A without a generic Stone/deficiency premise.
  CP10.g | exact_domains_evolution_and_core
    Prove graphwise U invariance, the integrated evolution identity, the maximal derivative and
    test-pairing domains, unique strong evolution and unique selfadjoint extension.
  CP10.h | resolvent_algebra_and_quantitative_core
    Derive adjoint, resolvent identity, commutativity, norm holomorphy, graph-tail estimates and
    actual C-infinity core approximants.
